articles.title: Email Suppression List Ownership — DKIM Domain Verification and Bounce Polling Setup
articles.excerpt: Put the email suppression list under platform control when setting up product event notifications, and make domain verification, DKIM, and bounce handling explicit release checks. For healthtech appoi…
articles.body: Put the email suppression list under platform control when setting up product event notifications, and make domain verification, DKIM, and bounce handling explicit release checks. For healthtech appointment reminders, the deciding constraint is template ownership: a team cannot safely change content if the same release silently changes which sender is authenticated or which invalid recipients become eligible again. Short answer: For a Node.js application sending product event notifications, keep domain verification and DKIM setup explicit, persist bounce decisions independently of templates, and make a polling worker commit those decisions before advancing its checkpoint. Use separate, explicitly selected US and EU processing contexts where the deployment requires them.

articles.title: CPR vs UG vs PDR: the flange detail that decides your waveguide VSWR
articles.excerpt: Two waveguide switches with identical electrical data, same band, same isolation — one sits in a system at VSWR 1.08, the other at 1.25. Nothing in the datasheet explains it. In most cases the differe…
articles.body: Two waveguide switches with identical electrical data, same band, same isolation — one sits in a system at VSWR 1.08, the other at 1.25. Nothing in the datasheet explains it. In most cases the difference is the flange. The four flange families you will actually meet UG (UG-385/U, UG-387/U and so on) — the classic MIL-spec flat flange with a defined bolt circle. Two UG flanges mate with a gasket or an O-ring in a groove, depending on the variant. Widely used in military and legacy radar hardware. CPR (CPR-90G, CPR-112G…) — "Cover, Pressurise, Rectangular". A flat cover flange with a gasket groove, designed so the joint can be pressurised. The letter suffix matters: G is grooved, F is flat, R is a choke flange. A CPR-G must mate with another CPR-G with a gasket.

Everything below is in docs/reports/benchmark-juice-shop.md and .json , and pnpm run:benchmark juice-shop --runs 3 reproduces it on a fresh Juice Shop (it needs Docker and no API key). The numbers are low. This text is about why they are low, what they do and do not mean, and what we did so they could not be flattered. Janus Arena has a Red Team that attacks a sandboxed copy of a target and a Blue Team that patches what it confirms. To say anything about the Red Team we needed a number from a target we do not control. We used OWASP Juice Shop (v20.3.0, pinned by digest), because it marks its own challenges as solved, which gives an oracle we did not write.

articles.title: Connector torque and repeatability: where 0.2 dB actually comes from
articles.excerpt: You tighten an SMA connector to what feels right, take a measurement, swap the cable, tighten it again, and the reading moves by 0.2 dB. Then you spend an afternoon hunting a "bad" component that was…
articles.body: You tighten an SMA connector to what feels right, take a measurement, swap the cable, tighten it again, and the reading moves by 0.2 dB. Then you spend an afternoon hunting a "bad" component that was never bad. The variation came from the connector, not the part. This is the most common source of unexplained scatter in RF work above about 8 GHz, and it is almost always a torque problem rather than a component problem. Why torque matters more than people expect An SMA interface is a precision lapped pair held together by thread friction. The centre pin contact depth is only a few tenths of a millimetre. Under-torque, and the outer conductor contact is not fully seated: you get a small series inductance and a reflection that grows with frequency.

articles.title: UX cost of a security patch
articles.excerpt: The UX cost of a security patch Janus Arena (November 2026). Every figure comes from real runs recorded in the project's event repository (docs/reports), A security fix is judged by one question: does…
articles.body: The UX cost of a security patch Janus Arena (November 2026). Every figure comes from real runs recorded in the project's event log: a brute-force fix on OWASP Juice Shop, and five Launch Day runs on ShopLab, a demo shop. The reports are in the repository ( docs/reports ), and the console's demo build replays two of the runs in your browser. The users are synthetic: language-model agents that play a person in a real browser. Nothing here is a conversion figure. A security fix is judged by one question: does the attack still work? It is a good question and it is not enough. A fix can stop the attack and also stop the people it was meant to protect, and the second half only shows up if you measure it.

articles.title: Containing Billing Credential Exposure in Scheduled Access Review Key Inventory Jobs
articles.excerpt: Schedule the access review with a credential that can read key metadata and cannot change billing settings. Keep the credential that replenishes a fintech service's prepaid balance outside that job, a…
articles.body: Schedule the access review with a credential that can read key metadata and cannot change billing settings. Keep the credential that replenishes a fintech service's prepaid balance outside that job, and archive each successful inventory as a dated document before declaring the run complete. TL;DR: An unattended key inventory should prove which identities could affect the balance, without giving the reporting process those same powers. A dated archive is evidence of an observation; it becomes access review evidence only when someone records a decision about that observation. The OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet supports the underlying controls: least privilege, lifecycle management, auditing, and automation.

articles.body: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to investigate the planet's missing water. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere.

articles.excerpt: The answer to one of Earth's greatest geological mysteries may lie deep beneath our feet.
articles.body: More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged.

articles.body: The Bravia 8 II has deep and inky blacks, giving great depth to space images. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights. Though, it turns out that you can already get a great deal on the 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II , one of our favorite OLED televisions. It’s currently discounted by $1,100 at various retailers, including Amazon , Best Buy , and directly from Sony . That discount brings the price under $2,200, the lowest we’ve seen. You can also save $800 on the 55-inch model, which is typically $2,599.99 ( Amazon , Best Buy , Sony ), but now costs just under $1,800.
